minutes.headline: Building committee asked school committee to help re-home extended day and TCP programs; no votes beyond adjournment.
minutes.summary: The committee met jointly with school committee members and heard the superintendent's response on where TCP programs (extended day, early learning center, community school links, ACE) could go if TCP is renovated or replaced. Members pressed for alternatives and asked the school committee for a position on future use of TCP, and a records-reduction effort. After the school members left, the committee reviewed a tracker of Vertex-identified building needs at Town Hall and Ritter, records storage plans, and next steps on reprioritizing space needs.

budget_items.what_was_said: About 12,500 square feet were committed for school functions in the remodel plan; at an assumed per-square-foot construction cost the chair estimated the school share at a few million dollars and said it would not pass.
The town recently approved money to purge and digitize records, expected to save square footage; the chair asked the school side to do similarly.
figures_as_heard: sixty two thousand five hundred dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said extended day is self-sustained by parent fees which pay staff; raising pay would raise fees. Later it was described as an enterprise account that also pays rent covering custodial costs.
The chair said a teardown and new build is ideal but a project of this size would not win voter approval.
A member said schools take about two-thirds of the budget; another member disputed it, saying it is closer to 60 percent and went down this year as a share of the omnibus.
A member said school-related capital was a small share last year and larger this year because of air conditioning for a school building.
Reducing storage need from a large figure at a per-square-foot cost multiplier would save millions.

decisions.decision: Chair asked the school committee to take a position on whether TCP should be preserved for future school use; school members said location matters less than resources and suggested exploring Turkey Hill first.
Chair will email the DiGiorgio space-needs worksheet to members; members to develop reprioritization criteria and 'king/queen for a day' layouts for the June 6 meeting.
Chair will send a communication to the select board about exploring record storage in the public safety attic.
Committee chose not to re-engage departments on space needs now, but to reprioritize first and then go back to departments.
Next meetings: June 6, then possibly a second June meeting to be discussed (June 20 not possible due to Juneteenth), and July 18.

what_happened.line: The committee took no votes; it met jointly with school committee members about where Town Campus Program (TCP) programs could go if the building is renovated or replaced.

The chair asked the school committee for a position on whether TCP should be kept for future school use; school members said resources matter more than location and suggested looking at Turkey Hill first.
Members discussed extended day, which the superintendent described as paid for by parent fees, and the roughly 12,500 square feet of school space in the remodel plan.
After the school members left, the committee reviewed capital work at Town Hall and Ritter and chose to reprioritize space needs before going back to departments.
The chair will write to the select board about records storage in the public safety attic; the next meetings are June 6 and July 18, with a possible second June date.

why_it_matters: Where the extended day and early learning programs end up decides how much school space any TCP renovation or replacement has to include, and that share feeds directly into what a future building article would ask voters to approve.
Extended day is paid for by parent fees, so a move or a change in rent or staff pay could change what families are charged rather than the tax bill.
watch_next: June 6 meeting: members bring reprioritization criteria and layouts for space needs.
The school committee's answer on whether TCP should be preserved for school use.
